newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha steadies as Skikda mystery unravelled.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha steadies as Skikda mystery unravelled.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices opened the week on a steady note as traders nervously watched Skikda loading schedules while mostly believing they would not have a significant impact on physical values.

Concerns that Algeria's state oil company Sonatrach's move last week to suspend double stem naphtha cargoes from loading out of Skikda would dump supplies onto Europe, appeared to be alleviated for now, they said.
But some traders said they were not completely sure what Sonatrach's stance was by Monday and therefore could not fully assess the impact on the Med and NWE markets.
They chose instead to focus on the steady crude prices.
Sonatrach was not immediately available on Monday for comment.
"We are not really worried," said one trader in the Mediterranean. "(Sonatrach) doesn't want to put things very clear but it seems to be only for the short term and a very short time."
Seasonal demand for gasoline should underpin the heavier naphtha grades and offset any bearish impact from Skikda, leaving the market relatively balanced, he said.
May swaps were up $2 at $179.50/$181.50 a tonne after an early bounce in crude oil, while June was heard traded at $182, up about $2.50 from Friday, traders said.
NWE cargoes were assessed roughly unchanged at $174/$176 cif with no deals heard done in early action.

"It's so difficult to understand what (Sonatrach) is playing," a NWE end-user said. He expected little local impact since "Northwest Europe is still well supplied...and even the tonnage that went last month to the Far East (from the Med) had no impact on NWE."
He pointed to Russian material available for early May as well as fob tonnage out of ARA.

Traders who had spoken to Sonatrach last week said the suspension was linked to the fact that jetty number three, the only one equipped for 60,000 tonne plus vessels, would be loading fuel oil through this week.
The other two berthing areas at Skikda are able to load up to 50,000 tonnes, sources said.
